There are a lot of nutty leftist takes out there but I find the rise of explicit amoral familism — overt arguments that the richest and most powerful people ought to behave more selfishly — to be really distressing and at odds with almost all of traditional western thought.

Suppose Mark Zuckerberg has seven more kids and then gives each of his ten children $2 billion each to live on. 

That seems like a lot of kids and a lot of money and still just a small share of his fortune — do something good with the rest!

What I find particularly odd about this thread is that beyond the baseline political malpractice, he’s not advocating that Democrats particularly *do* anything to address climate change.

If New England-based climate-pilled politicians like Whitehouse want to *act* more aggressively on climate change in a way that advances growth and affordability they could do this — nobody is stopping them except other environmentalists.

But broadly speaking there is always a case for *doing* politically inexpedient things in order to enact change in the world, but there’s no reason for senators to *talk* about things that don’t make it easier to win senate races in Alaska and Texas and Iowa and Ohio.

From a higher angle it’s just another squat five over one but I think it looks way better and it has a courtyard like a European block.

The adjoining neighborhood is a prison and a cemetery so I would say there is limited upside to this particular project, but if new infill in general looked like this I think we’d be in much better shape.
